items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1975-11-13
items.q: we three would do a Clark step like you said, the Austin Brothers does, if you ever listen to him, or Bill Robinson.

ctx.x: Yeah, I've heard of Harrison Hike.

So we three, when he would come back, we three would do a Clark step like you said, the Austin Brothers does, if you ever listen to him, or Bill Robinson. Yeah, yeah. We used to do all of these kind of things, you know. I had other little acts I would put in it. Streamline was an acrobat, and he taught me a little, you know, little tricks to the tree. I used to run up the wall, so high, three or four feet up a wall and turn around and come back down.
Did you do any jump through tumble salts or something, that kind of thing? Yeah.

items.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1969-05-30
items.q: We used to do something we got familiar with this dance through Bill Roberson.

ctx.x: You born in New Orleans now? No, I was born in Bugalooza. Bugalooza. And how old were you when you moved to New Orleans? Well, I was smart, I'm about two months old, my mother was. Two months old? Yeah. Yeah, that's pretty young. It's called, it's my own music. Yeah. I really don't know nothing about Bugalooza. Yeah. That isn't a good place, I know that. Bugalooza. Alright, when did you first get interested in music? Ever since you got a band?

No, I've been loving music because most of my people on both sides played in music. Like I said, I started off beating on these trumps and ten fans and things. I was around about seven, eight, nine years old. I wasn't making any money out of it, but we got kicks and it's fun, you know. Like little parties, at that time they had fish fries and things. I didn't make two, three dollars a piece, but I was playing money anyway. It was pretty impressive for us. So the guys got to telling me I met Lollipops in Memphis.…
You know you used to dance at the matinees.
